Abstract

braid group contains a braid whose standard closure is not integrally smoothly 1-solvable. Con-

papers.title: Failure of strong quadratic growth in unregularized sparse control of a critical wave equation
first_page_header_lines: Failure of strong quadratic growth in unregularized
sparse control of a critical wave equation
Alec Kriebel
October 14, 2026            (version 1.0)
Abstract
We give an explicit counterexample to retaining ordinary critical-cone strict positivity and
strong control-L2 quadratic growth after removing quadratic control regularization from the
energy-critical quintic-wave problem of Kunisch and Meinlschmidt. On the three-dimensional
unit ball, zero is the unique global optimizer for a suﬃciently small positive pointwise control cap.
Its ordinary critical cone is {0}, so the strict condition is vacuous, but feasible controls converging
in L∞ have objective gap o(kuk2L2 ). Nearby radial terminal targets admit global optimizers, and
every such optimizer has L2 displacement divided by target displacement tending to inﬁnity.
Local L1 quadratic growth survives. The construction realizes the established concentration and
noncoercivity mechanism in the actual nonlinear source model, using classical wave estimates.

papers.title: Generic Cantor actions of Z wr Z are hyperfinite
first_page_header_lines: Generic Cantor actions of Z o Z are hyperﬁnite
Alec Kriebel
Independent researcher
October 13, 2026 (version 1.0.0)
Abstract
We give an aﬃrmative answer to Question 3 in Iyer’s contribution, joint with Shinko, to
Oberwolfach Report 2/2025. A dense Gδ of continuous actions of the restricted wreath product
ZoZ on Cantor space has hyperﬁnite orbit equivalence relation on the entire space. We specialize
established Cantor-action lifting principles to obtain a continuous proﬁnite shift height. Finite-
width lamp slabs then satisfy the compatible-metric theorem of Conley–Jackson–Marks–Seward–
Tucker-Drob. The full preimage of the embedded integers is treated by a separate ﬁnite Borel
exhaustion. The auxiliary Borel theorem requires the height factor and allows stabilizers.
